messages:
elaine: Thanks all — quick follow-up thread for runtime questions from today
elaine: TL;DR: kernel work, batching/caching priorities, and where we expect perf wins in Q3. Ask here and we'll follow up with notes.
mike: Thanks! First q: how does continuous batching affect p50 vs p99? any rough numbers?
raj: short answer: p50 improves a lot for typical steady-state due to packing; p99 can improve but depends on request size variance and our dispatch thresholds. We saw p50 ~40% drop and p99 ~10-20% in our internal sims.
raj: longer: if lots of small requests we fill larger batches quickly -> big perf wins. If you have many long-seq requests they dominate GPU and p99 stays high unless we isolate via priority lanes.
sophia: can you explain "priority lanes" briefly?
raj: sure — we carve small higher-priority execution queues for latency-sensitive requests. they get dispatched with lower batching thresholds. tradeoff is lower throughput efficiency.
allison: any config knobs customers can use right now? e.g., set batch_delay_ms or priority flag?
raj: yes — in Dedicated and Private we expose batch_delay_ms, max_batch_tokens, and a priority boolean per route. Default autosuggests values but you can override. docs coming to /docs/runtime/batching next week.
elaine: kernel work Q: what kernel changes are most impactful?
liz: main things: fused attention kernels for shorter sequences, improved kv-cache memory layout to reduce memcpy, and int8 fast path for matmuls. Fused kernels give a big boost for chat-style short-context workloads.
mike: do we have canary plans for those kernels? worried about numerical regressions.
:infra-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime-kernels/v3 -> canary (eng-resources) at 2024-06-30T15:00Z
liz: yes canaries + unit/quantization validation + evals on our regression suite. We also gate int8 on quality thresholds per model.
sophia: nice. On caching: are we doing prefix caching only or KV-level dedup caches?
raj: both. prefix cache (request->response) is easiest for short repeated prompts. KV-level caching is per-layer key/value reuse for autoregressive generation. We're also exploring a small LRU across recent requests to catch prompt template reuse.
allison: how will this show up in Console? I want to see cache-hit rate per route.
:infra-bot: new metric: runtime.cache.hit_rate added to per-route dashboard
elaine: we'll add chart templates for cache-hit, batch-size distribution, and priority-lane utilization.
mike: any recommendations for developers building user-facing chat? e.g., strongly prefer shorter system prompts to help batching?
raj: yes keep system prompts compact or use server-side prompt-stitching so tokens counted for batching are minimized. Also prefer smaller max_tokens for interactive messages.
sophia: kernel perf question: do these fused kernels reduce memory usage or only compute?
liz: both. Fused kernels cut intermediate buffers and reduce total memory bandwidth. On A100 we saw ~15% less memory traffic for the fused attention path.
allison: rollout question: if a customer sees quality regressions after kernel update, what's the rollback path?
raj: automatic fallback to previous kernel variant per-model is enabled. We also have fast rollback of the canary fleet and a policy to pin a customer's traffic to a stable variant for 24h while we investigate.
elaine: thanks everyone — I'll pull these notes into the all-hands follow-up doc. if people want deeper dives, we'll spin up a tech chat next week with kernel owners. :thumbsup:
liz: happy to present microbenchmarks.
mike: +1 to a deep dive, thanks.
